### Tyre pressure monitoring
`suzuki_jimny_en_40d3df04` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:214 | doc_type:owners_manual
system (TPMS) (if equipped)
The tyre pressure monitoring system is
designed to alert you when one or more of
the tyres on your vehicle is significantly
under-inflated. The tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS) senso_r containing a
unique identification code 1s mounted on
each wheel. The TPMS sensors transmit
tyre pressure signals to the receiver of the
tyre pressure monitoring system controller.

### When the inflation pressure of one or more
`suzuki_jimny_en_fdc29632` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:214 | doc_type:owners_manual
tyres indicates significant under-inflation,
the low tyre pressure warning light shown
below comes on.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_697dff9a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:214 | doc_type:owners_manual
The word "telltale" in this section, means
an indicator.

### Low tyre pressure warning light
`suzuki_jimny_en_d9d5e3ab` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:215 | doc_type:owners_manual
(!)
52D305
Each tyre should be checked monthly
when cold and infiated to the infiation pressure recommended by the vehicle manu-
facturer on the vehicle placard or tyre
pressure label. (If your vehicle has tyres of
a different size than the size indicated on
the vehicle placard or tyre pressure label,
you should determine the proper tyre pressure for those tyres.)
As an added fuel efficiency feature, your
vehicle has been equipped with a tyre
pressure monitoring system (TPMS) that
illuminates a low tyre pressure telltale
when one or more of your tyres is significantly under-infiated.
Accordingly, when the low tyre pressure
telltale illuminates, you should stop and
check your tyres as soon as possible, and
infiate them to the proper pressure.
Driving on a significantly under-infiated
tyre causes the tyre to overheat and can
lead to tyre failure. Under-infiation also
reduces fuel efficiency and tyre tread life,
and may affect the vehicle's handling and
stopping ability.
Please note that the TPMS is not a substitute for proper tyre maintenance, and it is
the driver's responsibility to maintain correct tyre pressure, even if under-infiation
has not reached the level to trigger illumination of the TPMS low tyre pressure tell-
tale.

system
to

tyres can result in loss of control or

### To reduce the chance that the low tyre
`suzuki_jimny_en_b4c29d68` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:217 | doc_type:owners_manual
pressure warning light will come on due
to normal changes in temperature and
atmospheric pressure, it is important to
check and adjust the tyre pressures
when the tyres are cold. If you check
tyres after driving, they are warm. Even
if the tyre pressure seems to be good in
this condition, it could fall below the
specified pressure when tyres cool
down. Also, if tyres are inflated to the
specified pressure in a warm garage, the
tyre pressure could fall below the specified one when you drive the vehicle out-
side in very cold temperature. If you
adjust the tyre pressure in a garage that
is warmer than the outside temperature,
you should add 1 kPa to the recommended cold tyre pressure for every
O.B'C difference between garage temperature and outside temperature.

### Your vehicle has also been equipped with
`suzuki_jimny_en_5b887c91` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:218 | doc_type:owners_manual
a TPMS malfunction indicator to indicate
when the system is not operating properly.
The TPMS malfunction indicator is combined with the low tyre pressure telltale.
When the system detects a malfunction,
the telltale will flash for about 75 seconds
and then remain continuously illuminated.
This sequence will continue upon subsequent vehicle start-ups as long as the mal-
function exists.

### The TPMS malfunction indicator is not
`suzuki_jimny_en_c2e97be2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:218 | doc_type:owners_manual
reset even after the engine is turned off; it
remains in the ON state until the normal
conditions are restored.
When the malfunction indicator is illuminated, the system may not be able to
detect or signal low tyre pressure as
intended. TPMS malfunctions may occur
for a variety of reasons, including the
installation of replacement or alternate
tyres or wheels on the vehicle that prevent
the TPMS from functioning
properly.
Always check the TPMS malfunction telltale after replacing one or more tyres or
wheels on your vehicle to ensure the
replacement or alternation of tyres and
wheels to allow the TPMS to continue to
function properly.

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_4a108ebc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:224 | doc_type:owners_manual
Your multipurpose vehicle has handling characteristics that differ from
those of a conventional passenger
car. For the safety of you and your
passengers, please read the following section very carefully.

### SUZUKI have higher ground clearance
`suzuki_jimny_en_6130f0f0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:224 | doc_type:owners_manual
and a narrower track than conventional
passenger cars, to make them capable of
performing in a wide variety of off-road
applications. Specific design characteristics give them a higher center of gravity
than ordinary cars. An advantage of the
higher ground clearance is a better view of
the road allowing you to anticipate problems. They are not designed for cornering
at the same speed as conventional passenger cars any more than low-slung
sports cars are designed to perform satisfactorily under off-road conditions. If at all
possible, avoid sharp turns or abrupt
maneuvers. As with other vehicles of this
type, failure to operate this vehicle correctly may result in loss of control or vehi-
cle rollover. Multipurpose vehicles have a
significantly higher rollover rate than other
types of vehicles. In a rollover collision, an
unbelted person is significantly more likely
to die than a person wearing a seat belt.

### Higher Ground Clearance
`suzuki_jimny_en_4a4d5a39` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:224 | doc_type:owners_manual
The higher ground clearance of your vehicle enables it to clear off-road obstacles,
such as rocks and tree stumps, that ordinary passenger cars cannot drive over. An
unavoidable result of this higher ground
clearance is that the vehicle also has a
higher center of gravity. Consequently,
your vehicle will handle differently than a
vehicle with a lower center of gravity.

### Shorter Wheelbase
`suzuki_jimny_en_bb2b5d57` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:224 | doc_type:owners_manual
Along with its higher ground clearance,
your vehicle has a shorter wheelbase and
shorter front and rear overhangs than the
typical passenger car. These features
combine to allow you to drive your vehicle
over hillcrests without hanging up on them
or damaging the frame and chassis components. The shorter wheelbase also
makes the steering of your vehicle more
responsive than that of vehicles with longer wheelbases.

### Your vehicle is narrower than the average
`suzuki_jimny_en_ebed9858` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:225 | doc_type:owners_manual
passenger car so that it can pass through
tight spaces. Without the essential characteristics described above: higher ground
clearance, shorter wheelbase, and narrower body width and track -your vehicle
could not provide you with excellent offroad driving performance. However, it is
also true that on-road driving, handling,
and steering will be different from what
drivers experience with a conventional
passenger car.
On-Paved Road Driving
The data of accidents show that most rollover accidents for multi-purpose vehicles
are caused when a driver loses control of
the vehicle and leaves the paved portion of
the roadway striking a ditch, curb or other
off-road object that causes the vehicle to
overturn. The following driving practices
may reduce the risk of rollover.
Vehicle Slides Off-Road
You can reduce the risk of this kind of rollover accident by always keeping the vehi-
cle under control. Typically, drivers lose
control of vehicles, often resulting in rollover accidents, when the driver is impaired
because of alcohol or other drugs, falls
asleep at the wheel or is otherwise inattentive, or is driving too fast for the road con-
ditions.

### Rollovers On the Roadway
`suzuki_jimny_en_3c58b8ba` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:225 | doc_type:owners_manual
If, for any reason, your vehicle slides sideways or spins out of control at highway
speeds, while on the paved portion of the
roadway, the risk of rollover is greatly
increased. This condition can be created
when two or more wheels drop off onto the
shoulder and you steer sharply in an
attempt to reenter the roadway. To reduce
the risk of rollover in these circumstances,
if conditions permit, you should hold the
steering wheel firmly and slow down
before pulling back into the travel lanes
with controlled steering movements.

### All Types of Rollover Accidents
`suzuki_jimny_en_53819d16` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:225 | doc_type:owners_manual
б As with many kinds of automobile accidents, rollovers can be greatly reduced by
doing what all prudent drivers should do,
i.e., don't drink and drive, don't drive when
tired and don't do anything behind the
wheel that could cause a loss of attention
to the driving task.

### Additional guidelines are set out below for
`suzuki_jimny_en_dc3fb5ee` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:225 | doc_type:owners_manual
your on-road driving.
4-2
DRIVING TIPS
Know Your Vehicle

### Take time to familiarize yourself with the
`suzuki_jimny_en_3b60240d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:226 | doc_type:owners_manual
unique handling characteristics of your
vehicle by first driving around in an area
away from traffic. Practice turning the vehicle at a variety of speeds and in different
directions. Get a feel for the greater steering response that your vehicle has over a
conventional car.

### The driver and all passengers should be
`suzuki_jimny_en_9b833cce` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:226 | doc_type:owners_manual
properly restrained at all times, using the
seat belts provided. Refer to the "SEAT
BELTS" section for instructions on proper
use of the seat belts.
Don't Make Sharp Turns
As mentioned before, small multipurpose
vehicles have specific design characteristics that allow them to perform in a wide
variety of applications. These characteristics also change the cornering behavior
relative to conventional passenger cars.
Remember, small multipurpose vehicles
have more responsive steering and a
higher center of gravity than conventional
passenger cars. If at all possible, avoid
making sharp turns in your vehicle.
4-3

### Learn to approach curves cautiously and
`suzuki_jimny_en_32d5e974` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:226 | doc_type:owners_manual
at a conservative speed. Do not attempt to
take curves at the same speeds that you
would in a vehicle with a lower center of
gravity. Just as you would not drive a
sports car on a trail, you should not
attempt to drive your vehicle around
curves like a sports car.

### Under wet road conditions you should
`suzuki_jimny_en_0b58e160` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:226 | doc_type:owners_manual
drive at a lower speed than on dry roads
due to possible slippage of tyres during
braking. When driving on icy, snow-covered, or muddy roads, reduce your speed
and avoid sudden acceleration, abrupt
braking, or sharp steering movements.
Use 4-wheel drive high range (4H) for better traction.

### Never operate your vehicle in
`suzuki_jimny_en_33253951` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:227 | doc_type:owners_manual
114H" or
114L
11 on dry pavement and, as much
as possible, avoid using
114H" or

### 114L"
`suzuki_jimny_en_f6427b90` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:227 | doc_type:owners_manual
on wet pavement, as this puts severe
stress on the drive train, especially
during tight cornering, and can d~mage it. Also, you may have some d1ff1~
culty in steering.
Off-Road Driving
Your vehicle has specific design characteristics for off-road driving. When you leave
the paved road, you will encounter driving
surfaces of all kinds which may change
continually as you drive. In most cases, offroad driving requires the use of 4-wheel
drive.

### Always inspect hills before you attempt to
`suzuki_jimny_en_74ad4961` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:227 | doc_type:owners_manual
drive up them. Know what is on the other
side and how you will get back down. If
you have any doubt that it. is safe, do not
attempt to drive over a hill. Nev".r d_nve
your vehicle up an extremely steep incline.

### Coming down a steep hill can be trickier
`suzuki_jimny_en_ceb19464` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:227 | doc_type:owners_manual
than getting up one. Keep the vehicle
heading straight down the hill and use low
gear. Do not lock the brake~. If the vehicle
begins to slide, accelerate slightly to regain
steering control.

### Do not Drive Across the Side of
`suzuki_jimny_en_abf1f2ff` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:227 | doc_type:owners_manual
Hills
Driving across the side of a hill can be
extremely hazardous. Most of the vehicle'.s
weight will be transferred to the downhill
tyres, which could result in the vehicle rolling sideways. Whenever possible, avoid
this potential hazard. Also, 1f you have to
exit your vehicle on a side-hill, always get
out on the uphill side.

### You and your passengers should use the
`suzuki_jimny_en_49dc9394` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:227 | doc_type:owners_manual
seat belts at all times when driving offroad. For proper seat belt use, refer to the
"Seat Belts" section in this manual.
Avoid Sudden Reactions in Mud,
Ice, or Snow
Be careful when off-road conditions are
slippery. Reduce your speed and avoid
sudden movements of the vehicle. Be
aware that driving in deep snow or mud
can cause a loss of traction and an
increase in the resistance to the vehicle's
forward motion. Use 4WD low gear (4L)
and maintain a steady but moderate speed
with a light touch on the steering wheel
and brakes.
4-4

### Snow chains should only be used if they
`suzuki_jimny_en_7ff0646d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
are needed to increase traction or are
required by law. Check that the chains you
use are the correct size for your vehicle's
tyres.

### Also check that there is enough clearance
`suzuki_jimny_en_bd723ef9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
between the fenders and the chains as
installed on the tyres.
Install the chains on the rear tyres tightly,
according to the chain manufacturer's
instructions. Retighten the chains after
driving about 1.0 km (1/2 mile) if necessary. With the chains installed, drive slowly.

### If you hear the chains hitting against
`suzuki_jimny_en_8473f124` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
the vehicle body while driving, stop
and tighten them.
4-5

### Do not drive in the field covered
`suzuki_jimny_en_68afd54f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
with grown grass
If you drive in the field covered with grass,
it may cause accident or vehicle damage
by getting caught in grown grass.

### If Your Vehicle Gets Stuck
`suzuki_jimny_en_5df619b0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
If your vehicle gets stuck in snow, mud, or
sand, follow the directions below:

### 1) Shift the transfer shift lever into the "4L"
`suzuki_jimny_en_14ee46ff` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
position.
2) Shift the transmission back and forth
between a forward range (or first gear
for manual transmission) and reverse.

### This will create a rocking motion which
`suzuki_jimny_en_8b8be0a2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
may give you enough momentum to
free the vehicle. Press gently on the
accelerator to keep wheel spin to a minimum. Remove your foot from the
accelerator while shifting.
Do not race the engine. Excessive
wheel spin will cause the tyres to dig
deeper, making it more difficult to free
the vehicle.

### 3) If your vehicle remains stuck after a few
`suzuki_jimny_en_5dc78a07` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
minutes of rocking, get another vehicle
to pull you out.

### Do not allow anyone to stand near
`suzuki_jimny_en_ccd47039` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
the vehicle when you are rocking it,
and do not spin the wheels faster
than an indicated 40 km/h (25 mph)
on the speedometer. Personal injury
and/or vehicle damage may result
from spinning the wheels too fast.

### NOTICE
`suzuki_jimny_en_1706da4d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:228 | doc_type:owners_manual
• Release the accelerator pedal when
operating the gearshift lever or the
transfer lever. Operating the gearshift lever or the transfer lever with
the engine racing can damage the
gears and the free axle mechanism.
• Do not continue rocking the vehicle
for more than a few minutes. Prolonged rocking can cause engine
overheating, transmission, transfer case, axles, propeller shaft or
differential
damage, or tyre damage.

### In addition to following the driving

tips in this section, it is important to

condition and always maintain the
specified tyre pressure. Refer to
"Tyres"

DRIVING TIPS

### The purpose of the catalytic converter is to
`suzuki_jimny_en_b9d03d38` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:232 | doc_type:owners_manual
minimize the amount of harmful pollutants
in your vehicle's exhaust. Use of lead".d
fuel in vehicles equipped with catalytic
converters is prohibited, because lead
deactivates the pollutant-reducing components of the catalyst system.

### The converter is designed to last the life of
`suzuki_jimny_en_cfe0aee9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:232 | doc_type:owners_manual
the vehicle under normal usage and when
unleaded fuel is used. No special maintenance is required on the converter. How-
ever, it is very important to keep the engine
properly tuned. Engine misfiring, which can
result from an improperly tuned engine,
may cause overheating of the catalytic
converter. This may result in permanent
4-9
heat damage to the catalytic converter and
other vehicle components.

### NOTICE
`suzuki_jimny_en_37bb0f15` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:232 | doc_type:owners_manual
To mm,m,ze the possibility
of catalytic converter or other vehicle dam-
age:
• Maintain the engine in the proper
operating condition.
In the event of an engine malfunction,
particularly one
involving
engine misfire or other apparent
loss of performance, have the vehicle serviced promptly.
• Do not turn off the engine or interrupt the ignition when the t(ans~i~-
sion is in gear and the vehicle 1s m
motion.

### Do not try to start the engine by
`suzuki_jimny_en_003a504a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:232 | doc_type:owners_manual
pushing or towing the vehicle, or
coasting down a hill.

### Do not idle the engine with any
`suzuki_jimny_en_c00658f0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:232 | doc_type:owners_manual
spark plug wires disconnected or
removed, such as during diagnostic testing.
• Do not idle the vehicle for prolonged
periods
if idling
seems
rough or there are other malfunctions.

### Do not allow the fuel tank to get
`suzuki_jimny_en_12851b43` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:232 | doc_type:owners_manual
near the empty level.
A. WARNING
Be careful where you park and drive;
the catalytic
converter
and other
exhaust components
can get very
hot. As with any vehicle, do not park
or operate this vehicle in areas where
combustible
materials such as dry
grass or leaves can come in contact

### The following instructions will help you
`suzuki_jimny_en_9b45c91b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
improve fuel economy.
Avoid excessive idling
If you park your vehicle for more than one
minute, stop the engine and start it again
later. When warming up a cold engine, do
not allow the engine to idle or apply full
throttle until the engine has reached operating temperature. Allow the engine to
warm up by driving.

### Avoid fast starts
`suzuki_jimny_en_da13b3c4` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
F~st starts away from lights or stop signs
will consume fuel unnecessarily and
shorten engine life. Start off slowly.

### Avoid unnecessary stops
`suzuki_jimny_en_a2b89619` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
Avoid unnecessary deceleration and stopping. Try to maintain a moderate, steady
speed whenever possible. Slowing down
and then accelerating again uses more
fuel.

### Drive at a constant speed that road and
`suzuki_jimny_en_52b6195e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
traffic conditions will permit.
Keep the air cleaner clean

### 60A183
`suzuki_jimny_en_e1915454` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
If the air cleaner is clogged with dust, there
will be greater intake resistance, resulting
m decreased power output and increased
fuel consumption.

### Keep weight to a minimum
`suzuki_jimny_en_6999325b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
The heavier the load is, the more fuel the
vehicle consumes. Unload any unnecessary luggage or cargo.

### Keep tyre pressures correct
`suzuki_jimny_en_54cab70b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
Under-infiation of the tyres can waste fuel
due to increased rolling resistance of the
tyres. Keep your tyres infiated to the correct pressure shown in the label on driver's
door lock pillar.

### Highway driving
`suzuki_jimny_en_d5e6fe72` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
When driving at highway speeds, pay
attention to the following:
• Stopping
distance
progressively
increases with vehicle speed. Apply the
brakes far enough ahead of the stopping
prnnt to allow for the extra stopping distance.
On rainy days, hydroplaning can occur.

### Hydroplaning is the loss of direct contact
`suzuki_jimny_en_1b78e44d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:233 | doc_type:owners_manual
between the road surface and the vehicle's tyres due to a water film forming
between them. Steering or braking the
vehicle during hydroplaning can be very
difficult, and loss of control can occur.
Keep speed down when the road surface is wet.
At high speeds, the vehicle may be
affected
by side winds. Therefore,
reduce speed and be prepared for unexpected buffeting, which can occur at the
exits of tunnels, when passing by a cut
of a hill, or when being overtaken by
large vehicles, etc.
4-10

### 78RB04001
`suzuki_jimny_en_4571365d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:234 | doc_type:owners_manual

When driving on steep hills, the vehicle
may begin to slow down and show a lack
of power. If this happens, you should
shift to a lower gear so that the engine
will again be operating in its higher
power range. Shift rapidly to prevent the
vehicle from losing momentum.
When driving down a hill, the engine
should be used for braking by shifting to
the next lower gear.

### Do not hold the brake pedal down too
`suzuki_jimny_en_594ad42c` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:234 | doc_type:owners_manual
long or too often while going down a
steep or long hill. This could cause
the brakes to overheat, resulting in
reduced braking efficiency. Failure to
take this precaution could result in
loss of vehicle control.

`suzuki_jimny_en_434b5b60` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:249 | doc_type:owners_manual
of severe snowy, muddy or sandy
conditions, sudden starts or erratic
driving maneuvers which could
cause excessive stress on the
frame hook.
In such case, we recommend that
you contact a professional service.

### OTHER CONTROLS AND EQUIPMENT
`suzuki_jimny_en_f7cd1dc7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:255 | doc_type:owners_manual
Air conditioning switch (5)
To turn on the air conditioning system, set
the blower speed selector to a position
other than off and push in "NC" switch.
With this "NC" switch operation, a indicator light will come on when the air condi-
tioning system is working. To turn off the
air conditioning system, push "NC" switch
again.
During operation of the air conditioner, you
may notice slight changes in engine
speed. These changes are normal, the
system is designed so that the compressor
turns on or off to maintain the desired temperature.

### Less operation of the compressor results
`suzuki_jimny_en_b80d0549` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:255 | doc_type:owners_manual
in better fuel economy.
System operating instructions

### Natural ventilation
`suzuki_jimny_en_7586f0b9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:hvac | p:255 | doc_type:owners_manual
Select VENTILATION and FRESH AIR, the
temperature selector to the desired temperature position, and the blower speed
selector to off. Fresh air will flow through
the vehicle during driving.

### Forced ventilation
`suzuki_jimny_en_e01205dc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:hvac | p:255 | doc_type:owners_manual
The base settings are the same as for natural ventilation except you set the blower
speed selector to a position other than off.
Normal heating (using outside air)
Select HEAT and FRESH AIR, the temperature selector to the desired tempera-
ture position and the blower speed selector
to the desired blower speed position. Setting the blower speed selector to a higher
blower speed position increases heating
efficiency.
Quick heating (using recirculated air)
The base settings are the same as for normal heating except you select RECIRCU-
LATED AIR. If you use this heating method
for an extended period of time, the air in
the vehicle can become contaminated and
the windows can become misty. Therefore,
use this method only for quick heating and
change to the normal heating method as
soon as possible.
5-20

### OTHER CONTROLS AND EQUIPMENT
`suzuki_jimny_en_0792965b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
Head cooled/Feet warmed heating
Select BI-LEVEL and FRESH AIR, the
temperature selector to the desired temperature position, and the blower speed
selector to the desired blower speed position. Unless the temperature selector is in
the fully cold position or fully hot position,
the air that comes out of the center and
side outlets will be cooler than the air that
comes out of the floor outlets.

### Normal cooling
`suzuki_jimny_en_8d9eff5e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:hvac | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
Set the air flow selector to VENTILATION,
the temperature selector to the desired temperature position and the blower speed
selector to the desired blower speed position, and turn on "NG" switch. Setting the
blower speed selector to a higher blower
speed position increases cooling efficiency.

### You can switch the air intake selector to
`suzuki_jimny_en_70ec07f9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
either FRESH AIR or RECIRCULATED
AIR as you desire. Choosing RECIRCU-
LATED AIR increases cooling efficiency.
Quick cooling (using recirculated air)
The base settings are the same as for normal cooling except you select RECIRCU-
LATED AIR and the highest blower speed.

### If you select RECIRCULATED AIR for an
`suzuki_jimny_en_5038ccfc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
extended period of time, the air in the
vehicle can become contaminated and
the windows tend to get misted. Therefore, you should select FRESH AIR
whenever possible.
5-21

### If your vehicle has been left in the sun
`suzuki_jimny_en_d8df5355` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
with the windows closed, it will cool
faster if you open the windows briefly
while you operate the air conditioner with
the air intake selector at FRESH AIR
and the blower at high speed.

### Set the air flow selector to a desired air
`suzuki_jimny_en_092b9e03` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
flow selector position, the temperature
selector to the desired temperature position and the blower speed selector to the
desired blower speed position. Also select
FRESH AIR and turn on "NG" switch.

### Because the air conditioner dehumidifies
`suzuki_jimny_en_d7a45ee2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
the air, turning it on will help keep the windows clear, even when blowing heated air
using DEFROST or HEAT & DEFROST
functions.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_46641638` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:256 | doc_type:owners_manual
If you need maximum defrosting:
select DEFROST and FRESH AIR,
set the blower speed selector to high,
adjust the temperature selector to the
hot end,
turn on 'WC" switch, and
adjust the side outlets so the air blows
on the side windows.

### If you do not use the air conditioner for a
`suzuki_jimny_en_304da079` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:257 | doc_type:owners_manual
long period, such as during winter, it may
not give the best performance when you
start using it again. To help maintain optimum performance and durability of your air
conditioner, it needs to be run periodically.

### Operate the air conditioner at least once a
`suzuki_jimny_en_306df07b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:257 | doc_type:owners_manual
month for one minute with the engine
idling. This circulates the refrigerant and oil
and helps protect the internal components.

### If your air conditioner is equipped with air
`suzuki_jimny_en_423c7d3d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:257 | doc_type:owners_manual
filters, clean or replace them as specified
. in "Maintenance schedule" in "INSPEC-
TION AND MAINTENANCE" section.
(For models with air conditioner refrigerant R-1234yf)

### Your vehicle uses the air conditioning
`suzuki_jimny_en_ad2b526f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:257 | doc_type:owners_manual
refrigerant
HFO-1234yf,
commonly
called R-1234yf. R-1234yf replaced R-
134a for automotive applications. Other
refrigerants are available, but only R-
1234yf should be used in your vehicle.
(For the country of Singapore)
• For repair and parts replacement, have
your vehicle repaired or replaced parts
by an authorized SUZUKI dealer that
has the mechanic qualified with SAE
J2845 for air conditioner of R-1234yf.

### Using the wrong refrigerant may
`suzuki_jimny_en_8340a7dc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:257 | doc_type:owners_manual
damage your air conditioning system. Use R-1234yf only. Do not mix or
replace the R-1234yf with other refrigerants.
(For models with air conditioner refrigerant R-134a)

### Your vehicle uses the air conditioning
`suzuki_jimny_en_ad2b526f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:257 | doc_type:owners_manual
refrigerant HFC-134a, commonly called R-
134a. R-134a replaced R-12 around 1993
for automotive applications. Other refrigerants are available, including recycled R-12,
but only R-134a should be used in your
vehicle.

### Using the wrong refrigerant may
`suzuki_jimny_en_8340a7dc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:257 | doc_type:owners_manual
damage your air conditioning system. Use R-134a only. Do not mix or
replace the R-134a with other refrigerants.
5-22

introduced.

to manually turn the air conditioner on or off
according to your preference. When you
turn the air conditioning switch off, the climate control system cannot lower the inside
temperature below outside temperature.
To turn the climate control system off, push
"OFF" switch (7).

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_5a5269b6` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:263 | doc_type:owners_manual
If ''AUTO" in the display blinks, there is a
problem in the heating system and/or air
conditioning system. You should have the
system inspected by a SUZUKI dealer.

### To find the temperature at which you are
`suzuki_jimny_en_02bb2300` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:263 | doc_type:owners_manual
most comfortable, start with the 22'C
(72'F) or 25'C (75'F) setting. (the temperature vary depending on vehicle
specifications.).
If you turn the temperature selector (1)
until "HI" or "LO" appears on the display,
the climate control system will operate at
maximum heating or cooling and the
blower will run at full speed.

### To avoid blowing cold air in cold weather
`suzuki_jimny_en_101fa729` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:263 | doc_type:owners_manual
or hot air in hot weather, the system will
delay turning on the blower until warmed
or cooled air is available.

### If your vehicle has been left in the sun
`suzuki_jimny_en_de1717ee` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:263 | doc_type:owners_manual
with the windows closed, it will cool
faster if you open the windows briefly.
Even under the automatic operation, you
can set individual selectors to the manual
mode. The manually selected functions
are maintained, and the other functions
remain under automatic operation.
If the windshield and/or the front door
windows are fogged, push the defrost
switch (5) to turn on the defroster, or
push the air flow selector (4) to change
the air flow to HEAT & DEFROST position to defog the windows.
To return the blower speed selector (2),
air intake selector (3), and air flow selector (4) to automatic operation, push
''AUTO" switch (8).

### 78RB05049
`suzuki_jimny_en_1b99f7df` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:263 | doc_type:owners_manual
Be careful not to cover the interior temperature sensor (10) located between the
steering wheel and the climate control
panel, or the solar sensor (11) located at
the top of the passenger's side dashboard.

### These sensors are used by the automatic
`suzuki_jimny_en_3ea7ec89` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:sensors | p:263 | doc_type:owners_manual
system to regulate temperature.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_ba998902` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:264 | doc_type:owners_manual

### If you pay too much attention to
`suzuki_jimny_en_5d90f567` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:267 | doc_type:owners_manual
operating the audio system or viewing the audio system display while
driving, an accident can occur. If
you set the sound volume too loud,
it could prevent you from being
aware of road and traffic conditions.
• Keep your eyes on the road and
your mind on the drive. Avoid paying too much attention to operat-
ing the audio system or viewing
the audio system display.

### Familiarize yourself with the audio

presets.

`suzuki_jimny_en_cffd62a4` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:267 | doc_type:owners_manual

be aware of road and traffic conditions while driving.

### When the inside of the vehicle is very
`suzuki_jimny_en_a0473ef7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:hvac | p:267 | doc_type:owners_manual
cold and the player is used soon after
switching on the heater, condensation
may form on the disc or the optical
parts of the player and proper playback
may not be possible. If condensation
forms on the disc, wipe it off with a soft
cloth. If condensation forms on the optical parts of the player, do not use the
player for about one hour. This will
allow the condensation to disappear
normally.

### Driving on extremely bumpy roads
`suzuki_jimny_en_6d8a029b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:267 | doc_type:owners_manual
which cause severe vibrations may
cause sound to skip.

Even in the event that trouble arises,
never open the case, disassemble the
unit, or lubricate the rotating parts.
Bring the unit to a SUZUKI dealer.

Notes on MP3/WMA/AAC
What is MP3?
An abbreviation of "MPEG audio layer3",
MP3 is an audio compression format
that has become the standard format
among PC users. Its merit is that the
original audio data is compressed to
approximately 1/10 and high sound quality is maintained. This means that it is
possible to store the data of approximately 1 0 music CDs on a single CD-R/
RW disc, which in turn makes it possible
to play music for a long time without having to change the disc.
WhatisWMA?
An abbreviation of "Windows Media
Audio," WMA is an audio compression
format developed by Microsoft.
WMA files for which the ORM (Digital
Rights Management) function is on cannot be played.
Windows Media™ and the Windows®
logo are trademarks or registered trademarks of Microsoft Corporation in the
United States and other countries.
What isAAC?
An abbreviation of "Advanced Audio
Coding," AAC is an audio compression
format used by MPEG2 and MPEG4.
Points to remember when making MP3/
WMA/AAC files

### Common
`suzuki_jimny_en_efef86b1` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:288 | doc_type:owners_manual
High bit rate and high sampling frequency are recommended for high qual-
ity sounds.
Selecting VBR (Variable Bit Rate) is not
recommended. Selecting VBR
may
cause display of incorrect playing time
and jumpiness of playback.
Playback sound quality varies depending on the encoding environment. For
details, refer to the user manual of the
encoding software and the writing software in use.

### Never use

them in different folders.

Turn "VOL PUSH PWR" knob (2) while a
call is coming in.
Turning it clockwise increases the volume;
turning
it
counterclockwise
decreases the volume.
Press "VOL" switch (10) during a call.
Pressing the switch up increases the volume;
pressing
the
switch
down
decreases the volume.

to increase until the switch is released.
To decrease the volume, press the

continue to decrease until the switch is
released.
To mute the sound, press the switch (2).

### It is possible to turn on the audio system
`suzuki_jimny_en_8bbc7d12` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:310 | doc_type:owners_manual

Selecting the radio station (AM, FM1,
FM2, DAB1, DAB2 mode)
To select the next preset station, press
">" of the switch (4) only for a moment.
To select the previous preset station,
press "<" of the switch (4) only for a
moment.
To scan a higher frequency radio station,
press ">" of the switch (4) for 1 second
or longer.
To scan a lower frequency radio station,
press "<" of the switch (4) for 1 second
or longer.
Selecting the track (CD, USB (iPod),
Bluetooth® audio mode)
To skip to the next track, press ">" of the
switch (4) only for a moment.
To skip to the previous track, press "<" of
the switch (4) twice only for a moment.
When the switch (4) is pushed down
once only for a moment, the track currently being played will start from the
beginning again.
Fast forwarding/rewinding a track
To fast forward a track, press ">" of the
switch (4) for 1 second or longer.
To fast rewind a track, press "<" of the
switch (4) for 1 second or longer.

### 78RB05067
`suzuki_jimny_en_baea8f88` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:311 | doc_type:owners_manual
The anti-theft function is intended to discourage thefts. For example, when the
audio system is installed in another vehicle, it will become unable to operate.

### This function works by entering a Personal
`suzuki_jimny_en_dda267cd` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:311 | doc_type:owners_manual
Identification Number (PIN).
When the unit is disconnected from its
power source, such as when the audio
system is removed or the lead-acid battery
is disconnected, the unit will become inoperable until the PIN is reentered.
5-76

### OTHER CONTROLS AND EQUIPMENT
`suzuki_jimny_en_213755c1` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
Setting the anti-theft function
1) Press "VOL PUSH PWR" knob (1) to
power off.

### 2) Hold down the buttons numbered [1]
`suzuki_jimny_en_c1d0f6a5` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
and [6] of PRESET buttons (2) and
press "VOL PUSH PWR" knob (1).
"SECURITY" will be displayed.

### 3) Press UP button (3) and the button
`suzuki_jimny_en_a80d1bc7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
numbered [1] of PRESET buttons (2)
simultaneously.
4) Enter a 4-digit number to be registered
as PIN using the buttons numbered [1]
- [4] of PRESET buttons (2).

### 5) Hold
`suzuki_jimny_en_67f1958e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
down
"TUNE/FLO
PUSH
SOUND" knob (4) for 1 second or longer to set the anti-theft function.

### Take a note of the registered PIN and keep
`suzuki_jimny_en_2b561ac5` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
it for the future use.
5-77
Canceling the anti-theft feature
To cancel the anti-theft function, delete the
registered PIN.

### 1) Press "VOL PUSH PWR" knob (1) to
`suzuki_jimny_en_b09ca434` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
power off.
2) Hold down the buttons numbered [1]
and [6] of PRESET buttons (2) and
press "VOL PUSH PWR" knob (1).
"PIN ENTRY" will be displayed.

### 5) Hold
`suzuki_jimny_en_67f1958e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
down
"TUNE/FLO
PUSH
SOUND" knob (4) for 1 second or longer to delete the registered PIN. The
indication "---" will be displayed and
the anti-theft function will be canceled.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_09abc128` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
To change your PIN, first delete your current PIN, and then set a new one.

### Confirming the Personal Identification
`suzuki_jimny_en_5835eff9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
Number (PIN)
When the main power source is disconnected such as when the lead-acid battery
is replaced, etc. it is required to enter the
PIN to operate the unit again.

### 1) Set the ignition switch to "ACC" posi-
`suzuki_jimny_en_6521a7d1` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
tion.
"SECURITY" will be displayed.
2) Press UP button (3) and the button
numbered [1] of PRESET buttons (2)
simultaneously.

### 3) Enter a 4-digit number to be registered
`suzuki_jimny_en_ac09527e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
as PIN using the buttons numbered [1]
- [4] of PRESET buttons (2).

### 4) Hold
`suzuki_jimny_en_383bc688` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
down
"TUNE/FLO
PUSH
SOUND" knob (4) for 1 second or longer.

### When the same PIN as registered is
`suzuki_jimny_en_eb0e1411` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
entered, the power of the audio system
will be turned off automatically and it
will become operable again.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_09abc128` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:312 | doc_type:owners_manual
If an incorrect PIN is entered, "ERROR"
and the total number of incorrect entry

### .A. WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_8a5629ab` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:318 | doc_type:owners_manual
Take extreme care when working ПОб
your vehicle to prevent accidental
injury. Carefully observe the following precautions:
• To prevent damage or unintended
activation of the airbag system or
seat belt pretensioner system, check
that the lead-acid battery is disconnected and the ignition switch has
been in "LOCK" position for at least
90 seconds before performing any
electrical service work on your
SUZUKI vehicle. Do not touch airbag
system components, seat belt pretensioner system components or
wires.

### The wires are wrapped with yellow
`suzuki_jimny_en_ab4c65f2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:318 | doc_type:owners_manual
tape or yellow tubing, and the couplers are yellow for easy identifica-
tion.

garages or other confined areas.
(Continued)
6-1
.A. WARNING
(Continued)
When the engine is running, keep
hands, clothing, tools, and other
objects away from the fan and drive
belt. Even though the fan may not
be moving,
it can automatically
turn on without warning .
• When it is necessary to perform
service work with the engine run~
ning, check that the parking brake
is set fully and the transmission is
in Neutral (for manual transmission
vehicles)
or Park (for automatic
transmission vehicles).

the engine or when the engine is

not to touch
a hot
engine,
exhaust
manifold
and
pipes, muffler, radiator and water
hoses.
Do not allow smoking, sparks, or
flames around fuel or the battery.
Flammable fumes are present.

INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE
Maintenance recommended under severe driving conditions (except for EU countries and Israel)
Follow this schedule if your vehicle is mainly operated under one or more of the following conditions:
• When most trips are less than 6 km (4 miles).
• When most trips are less than 16 km (10 miles) and outside temperature remains below freezing.
Idling and/or low-speed operation in stop-and-go traffic.
Operating in extremely cold weather and/or on salted roads.
Operating in rough and/or muddy areas.
Operating in dusty areas.
Repeated high speed drive or high engine revolutions.
Towing a trailer, if admitted.
Schedule should also be followed if the vehicle is used for delivery service, police, taxi or other commercial applications.
NdTE:
For the Maintenance Recommended under Severe Driving Conditions of Russian models, refer to "For Russia" in the "SUPPLEMENT"
section.

INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE
Maintenance recommended under severe driving conditions (for EU countries and Israel)
Follow this schedule if your vehicle is mainly operated under one or more of the following conditions:
• When most trips are less than 6 km (4 miles).
When most trips are less than 16 km (1 O miles) and outside temperature remains below freezing.
Idling and/or low-speed operation in stop-and-go traffic.
Operating in extremely cold weather and/or on salted roads.
Operating in rough and/or muddy areas.
Operating in dusty areas.
Repeated high speed drive or high engine revolutions.
Towing a trailer, if admitted.
Schedule should also be followed if the vehicle is used for delivery service, police, taxi or other commercial applications.

### 52D084
`suzuki_jimny_en_61163257` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:341 | doc_type:owners_manual
6-24
INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE
It is important to keep the engine oil at the
correct level for proper lubrication of your
vehicle's engine. Check the oil level with
the vehicle on a level surface. The oil level
indication may be inaccurate if the vehicle
is on a slope. The oil level should be
checked either before starting the engine
or at least 5 minutes after stopping the
engine.
The handle of the engine oil dipstick is colored with yellow for easy identification.
6-25
Pull out the oil dipstick, wipe the oil off with
a clean cloth, insert the dipstick all the way
into the engine, and then remove it again.

### The oil on the stick should be between the
`suzuki_jimny_en_567c1426` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:342 | doc_type:owners_manual
upper and lower limits shown on the stick.
If the oil level indication is near the lower,
limit, add enough oil to raise the level to
the upper limit.

### Failure to check the oil level regularly
`suzuki_jimny_en_7975efd0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:342 | doc_type:owners_manual
could lead to serious engine trouble
due to insufficient oil.

### Remove the oil filler cap and pour oil slowly
`suzuki_jimny_en_e2387f41` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:342 | doc_type:owners_manual
through the filler hole to bring the oil level
to the upper limit on the dipstick. Be careful
not to overfill the oil. Too much oil is almost
as bad as too little oil. After refilling, start the
engine and allow it to idle for about a minute. Stop the engine, wait about 5 minutes
and check the oil level again.

### Drain the engine oil while the engine is still
`suzuki_jimny_en_b77c99b6` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:343 | doc_type:owners_manual
warm.
78RB07003
1) Remove the oil filler cap.
2) Place a drain pan under the drain plug.

### 3) Using a wrench, remove the drain plug
`suzuki_jimny_en_9db3922e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:343 | doc_type:owners_manual
and drain the engine oil.
A CAUTION
The engine oil temperature may be
high enough to burn your fingers
when the drain plug is loosened. Wait
until the drain plug is cool enough to
touch with your bare hands.
Tightening torque for drain plug:
35 Nm (3.6 kg-m, 25.8 lb-ft)

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_fc423047` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:343 | doc_type:owners_manual
Engine oil can be hazardous. Children and pets may be harmed by
swallowing
new or used oil. Keep
new and used oil and used oil filters
away from children and pets.
Repeated, prolonged
contact
with
used engine oil may cause skin cancer.
Brief contact with used oil may irritate skin.
(Continued)

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_fc423047` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:343 | doc_type:owners_manual
(Continued)
To minimize your exposure to used
oil, wear a long-sleeve shirt and
moisture-proof gloves (such as dishwashing gloves) when changing oil. If
oil contacts your skin, wash thoroughly with soap and water.

### Launder any clothing or rags if it is
`suzuki_jimny_en_c7397fe0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:343 | doc_type:owners_manual
with oil.
Recycle or properly dispose of used
oil and oil filters.

ket. Tighten the plug with a wrench to
the specified torque.

recommended that you use a genuine SUZUKI replacement filter. If
you use an aftermarket filter, check

• Oil leakage from the periphery of

incorrect
installation
or
gasket
damage. If you find any leakage or

### NOTICE
`suzuki_jimny_en_e3a25cda` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual

### To maintain optimum performance and
`suzuki_jimny_en_ac626888` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
durability of your engine, use SUZUKI genuine coolant or equivalent.

### If you use the engine coolant other than
`suzuki_jimny_en_d4171c12` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
the SUZUKI LLC: Super (Blue) for replacement, follow the schedule of SUZUKI LLC:
Standard (Green). To see the detail of the
maintenance schedule, refer to "Periodic
maintenance schedule" in this section.

### This type of coolant is the best for cooling
`suzuki_jimny_en_6abd3675` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
system for the following reasons:
• The coolant helps maintain proper
engine temperature.
It gives proper protection against freezing and boiling.
It gives proper protection against corrosion and rust.

### INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE
`suzuki_jimny_en_bbbf8d75` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
Failure to use the proper coolant can damage your cooling system. Your SUZUKI
dealer can help you select the proper coolant.

### NOTICE
`suzuki_jimny_en_e3a25cda` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
To avoid damaging your cooling system:
Always use a high quality ethylene
glycol base non-silicate type coolant diluted with distilled water at
the correct mixture concentration.
Check that the proper mix is 50/50
coolant to distilled water and in no
case higher than 70/30. Concentrations greater than 70/30 coolant to
distilled water will cause overheating conditions.

### Do not use straight coolant nor
`suzuki_jimny_en_b6d35f07` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
plain water (except "SUZUKI LLC:
Super {Blue)").
.
• Do not add extra inhibitors or additives. They may not be compatible
with your cooling system.

### Do not mix different types of base
`suzuki_jimny_en_39f99321` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:345 | doc_type:owners_manual
coolants. Doing so may result in
accelerated seal wear and/or the
possibility of severe overheating
and
extensive
engine/automatic
transmission damage.

product and contributes to the desired

`suzuki_jimny_en_0a840c18` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:346 | doc_type:owners_manual

### 78RB07005
`suzuki_jimny_en_bc8c850a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:346 | doc_type:owners_manual
If the coolant level is below "LOW" mark,
coolant should be added. While the engine
is cool, remove the reservoir tank cap and
add coolant until the reservoir tank level
reaches "FULL" mark. Never fill the reservoir tank above "FULL" mark.

### NOTICE
`suzuki_jimny_en_ae24a9f5` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:346 | doc_type:owners_manual
When putting the cap on the reservoir tank, line up the mark on the cap
and the mark on the tank. Failure to
follow this can result in coolant leakage.

### 78RB07014
`suzuki_jimny_en_5fa9c549` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
To change a wheel, use the following procedure:
1) Remove the jack, tools and spare
wheel from the vehicle.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_4dd246c4` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
How to remove the spare wheel:
78RB07052
1. Remove the center nut (1 ), then
remove the spare wheel half cover
(2) (if equipped).

### 2. Remove the wheel nuts of the spare
`suzuki_jimny_en_56b19fc8` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
wheel, then remove the spare wheel
with both hands.

### 2) Loosen, but do not remove the wheel
`suzuki_jimny_en_18428bbc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
nuts.
3) Jack up the vehicle (follow the jacking
instructions in the "EMERGENCY SER-
VICE" section in this manual)

### 5) Before installing the new wheel, clean
`suzuki_jimny_en_2c1c8f3c` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
any mud or dirt off from the surface of
the wheel and hub with a clean cloth.
Clean the hub carefully; it may be hot
from driving.

### 6) Install the new wheel and replace the
`suzuki_jimny_en_f24ee856` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
wheel nuts with their cone shaped end
facing the wheel. Tighten each nut
snugly by hand until the wheel is
securely seated on the hub.

### 78RB07017
`suzuki_jimny_en_06533e31` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
Tightening torque for wheel nut:
100 Nm (10.0 kg-m, 72.3 lb-ft)

### 7) Lower the jack and fully tighten the nuts
`suzuki_jimny_en_1bd37bd4` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
in a crisscross fashion with a wrench as
shown in the illustration.

### Use genuine wheel nuts and tighten
`suzuki_jimny_en_9514e50a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
them to the specified torque as soon
as possible after changing wheels.

### Incorrect wheel nuts or improperly
`suzuki_jimny_en_6ec53865` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
tightened wheel nuts may come
loose or fall off, which can result in
an accident. If you do not have a
torque wrench, have the wheel nut
torque checked by a SUZUKI dealer.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_8dbd278e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual

(3)

removal. For vehicles equipped with the

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_95a8c903` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:358 | doc_type:owners_manual
• Batteries
produce
flammable
hydrogen gas. Keep flames and
sparks away from the battery or an
explosion may occur. Never smoke
when working near the battery.
• When checking or servicing the
battery, disconnect the negative
cable. Be careful not to cause a
short circuit by allowing metal
objects to contact the battery posts
and the vehicle at the same time.
To avoid harm to yourself or damage to your vehicle or battery, fol-
low the jump-starting instructions
in "EMERGENCY SERVICE" section if it is necessary to jump-start
your vehicle.
• Diluted sulfuric acid spilled from
battery can cause blindness or
severe burns. Use proper eye protection and gloves. Flush eyes or
bodi,: with ample water and get
medical care immediately if suffered. Keep batteries out of reach
of children.

For maintenance-free battery (cap-less
type), you need not add water. For traditional type battery, which has water filler
caps, the level of the battery fluid (acid)
fluid (acid) must be kept between the
upper level line (1) and lower level line (2)
at all times. If the level is found to be below
the lower level line (2), add distilled water
to the upper level line (1 ). You should periodically check the battery, battery termi-
nals, . and battery hold-down bracket for
corrosion. Remove corrosion using a stiff
brush and ammonia mixed with water or
baking soda mixed with water. After
removing corrosion, rinse with clean water.

from the negative terminal of the battery to
help prevent discharge.

of the vehicle's functions will be initialized and/or deactivated.

### These functions must be required to
`suzuki_jimny_en_1b309c06` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual
reset after the battery is reconnected.
Do not disconnect the battery terminals
for at least one minute after the ignition
switch is turned off.

### Batteries contain toxic substances
`suzuki_jimny_en_cea750c7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual
including sulfuric acid and lead. They
could have potential negative consequences for the environment and
human health. Used batteries must
be disposed of or recycled according
to applicable rules or regulations and
must not be disposed of with ordinary household trash. Make sure not
to tip over the battery when you
remove it from the vehicle. Otherwise, sulfuric acid could run out and
you might get injury.

and system are operated for a while.

after turning the ignition switch to

The crossed-out wheeled bin symbol (5)
located on the battery label indicates that
the used battery should be collected separately from ordinary household trash. The
chemical symbol of "Pb" (6) indicates the
battery contains more than 0.004% lead.

### By ensuring the used battery is disposed
`suzuki_jimny_en_96b9abbb` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual
of or recycled correctly, you will help prevent potential negative consequences for
the environment and human health, which
could otherwise be caused by inappropriate trash handling of the battery. The recy-
cling of materials will help to conserve
natural resources. For more detailed information about disposing of or recycling the
used battery, consult a SUZUKI dealer.

### INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE
`suzuki_jimny_en_aaa90767` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual
Fuses
Your vehicle has three types of fuses, as
described below:

### The main fuse takes current directly from
`suzuki_jimny_en_3ec76a2e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual
the lead-acid battery.
Primary fuses
These fuses are between the main fuse
and individual fuses, and are for electrical
load groups.

### Individual fuses
`suzuki_jimny_en_c2c9bb52` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual
These fuses are for individual electrical circuits.
To remove a fuse, use the fuse puller provided in the fuse box cover.

The main fuse, primary fuses and some of
the individual fuses are located in the
engine compartment. If the main fuse
blows, no electrical component will function. If a primary fuse blows, no electrical
component in the corresponding load
group will function. When replacing the
main fuse, a primary fuse or an individual
fuse, use a genuine SUZUKI replacement
parts or equivalent for individual fuses.
To remove a fuse, use the fuse puller provided in the fuse box. The amperage of
each fuse is shown in the back of the fuse
box cover.

### If the main fuse or a primary fuse
`suzuki_jimny_en_751623f6` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:361 | doc_type:owners_manual
blows, have your vehicle inspected
by a SUZUKI dealer. Always use a
genuine SUZUKI replacement. Never
use a substitute such as a wire even
for a temporary repair, or extensive
electrical damage and a fire can
result.

### Check that the fuse box always carries
`suzuki_jimny_en_46359ff4` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:361 | doc_type:owners_manual
spare fuses.

`suzuki_jimny_en_681e6a49` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:363 | doc_type:owners_manual

### Light bulbs can be hot enough to
`suzuki_jimny_en_b5ad5ffe` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
burn your finger right after turning
off lights. This is true especially for
halogen headlight bulbs. Replace
the bulbs after they become cool
enough.

### The headlight bulbs are filled with
`suzuki_jimny_en_245999c3` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
pressurized halogen gas. They can
burst and injure you if they are hit
or dropped. Handle them carefully.

### To avoid
`suzuki_jimny_en_aee9283d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
injury
by sharp-edged
parts of the body, wear gloves and
a long-sleeved shirt when replacing
light bulbs.

### The oils from your skin may cause a
`suzuki_jimny_en_339193f2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
halogen bulb to overheat and burst
when the lights are on. Grasp a new
bulb with a clean cloth.

### Frequent bulb replacement indicates
`suzuki_jimny_en_742fe7db` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
the need for an inspection of the electrical system. This should be carried
out by a SUZUKI dealer.

Jacking instructions
75F062
1) Place the vehicle on level, hard ground.

### 2) Set the parking brake firmly and shift
`suzuki_jimny_en_dc2fcfd3` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
into "P" (Park) if your vehicle has an
automatic transmission, or shift int6 "R"
(Reverse) if your vehicle has a manual
transmission.

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_9b7687e2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
Shift into "P" (Park) for an automatic
transmission, or into "R" (Reverse)
for a manual transmission vehicle
when you jack up the vehicle.
• Never jack up the vehicle with the
transmission in
11N" (Neutral). Otherwise, unstable jack may cause an
accident.

### 3) Turn on the hazard warning switch if
`suzuki_jimny_en_c24a6054` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
your vehicle is near traffic.
4) Block the front and rear of the wheel
diagonally opposite of the wheel being
lifted.

### 5) Place the spare wheel near the wheel
`suzuki_jimny_en_cd6c58df` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
being lifted as shown in the illustration
in case that the jack is slipped.
Front wheel/Rear wheel

### 54G277
`suzuki_jimny_en_533f3df6` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:379 | doc_type:owners_manual
(1) Boss
6) Position the jack vertically and raise the
jack by turning the jack handle clockwise until the jack head hole fits into the
boss (1) of the body as the illustration.

### 7) Continue to raise the jack slowly and
`suzuki_jimny_en_547cbe6b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:379 | doc_type:owners_manual
smoothly until the tyre clears the
ground. Do not raise the vehicle more
than necessary.

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_800b8684` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:379 | doc_type:owners_manual
• Use the jack only to change wheels
on level, hard ground.
• Never jack up the vehicle on an
inclined surface.
• Never raise the vehicle with the
jack
in
a location
other
than
between the frame bosses near the
wheel to be changed.
• Make sure that the jack is raised at
least 51 mm (2 inches) before it
contacts the boss. Use of the jack
when it is within 51 mm (2 inches)
of being fully collapsed may result
in failure of the jack.
No person should place any portion of their body under a vehicle
that is supported by a jack.
• Never run the engine when the
vehicle is supported
by the jack
and never allow
passengers
to
remain in the vehicle.

Jump-starting instructions

### A. WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_15887e53` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
Never attempt to jump-start your
vehicle
if the
lead-acid
battery
appears to be frozen. Batteries in
this condition may explode.
When making jump lead connections, check that your hands and
the jump leads remain clear from
pulleys, belts or fans.
Lead-acid batteries produce flammable hydrogen gas. Keep flames
and sparks away from the battery
or an explosion may occur. Never
smoke when working near the battery.

### If the booster battery you use for
`suzuki_jimny_en_022d07ba` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
jump-starting is installed in another
vehicle, check that the two vehicles
are not touching each other.
If your lead-acid battery discharges
repeatedly, for no apparent reason,
have your vehicle inspected by a
SUZUKI dealer.
• To avoid harm to yourself or damage to your vehicle or battery, fol-
low the jump-starting
instructions
below.
If you are in doubt, call for qualified
road service.

### Your vehicle should not be started by
`suzuki_jimny_en_79a88abd` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
pushing
or towing.
This
starting
method could result in permanent
damage to the catalytic converter.

### Use jump leads to start a vehicle with
`suzuki_jimny_en_6a214e20` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
a weak or flat battery.
1) Use only a 12-volt lead-acid battery to
jump-start your vehicle. Position the
good 12-volt lead-acid battery close to
your vehicle so that the jump leads will
reach both batteries. When using a battery installed on another vehicle, check
that two vehicles do not touch each
other. Set the parking brakes fully on
both vehicles.

### 2) Turn off all vehicle accessories, except
`suzuki_jimny_en_5e55e03d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
those necessary for safety reasons (for
example, headlights or hazard lights).

### 1. Connect one end of the first jump
`suzuki_jimny_en_a7c2800f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
lead to the positive (+) terminal of
the discharged battery (1 ).

### 2. Connect the other end to the positive
`suzuki_jimny_en_10db6f74` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
(+) terminal of the booster battery
(2).
3. Connect one end of the second jump
lead to the negative (-) terminal of
the booster battery (2).

### 4. Make the final connection to an
`suzuki_jimny_en_e43796a9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
unpainted metal part (3) of engine
cylinder head in the vehicle with the
discharged battery (1 ).

### Never connect the jump lead directly
`suzuki_jimny_en_31121ea5` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
to the negative (-) terminal of the discharged battery, or an explosion may
occur.

### 4) If the booster battery you are using is
`suzuki_jimny_en_7e411bff` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
fitted to another vehicle, start the
engine of the vehicle with the booster
battery. Run the engine at moderate
speed.

### 5) Start the engine of the vehicle with the
`suzuki_jimny_en_c661eb53` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
discharged battery.
6) Remove the jump leads in the exact
reverse order in which you connected
them.

### Towing your vehicle
`suzuki_jimny_en_7f2f13e5` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
(recreational towing)

`suzuki_jimny_en_fc84590e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual

the instructions below to avoid accidents and damage to your vehicle. In
addition, be sure to observe government and local requirements regard-
ing vehicle lighting and trailer hitches
or tow bars.

when you tow your vehicle.
NOTICE

sensor brake support, if your vehicle
is towed with the engine on, press
dual

brake

### OFF

switch and turn off the dual sensor
brake
support.

not,

### Observe the following
`suzuki_jimny_en_2c30860a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:384 | doc_type:owners_manual
instructions
when towing your vehicle.
To help avoid damage to your vehicle during towing, proper equip-
ment and towing procedures must
be used.
• Using the frame hook, tow your
vehicle on paved roads for short
distances at low speed.

### If you tow your vehicle with the front

wheels on the ground, shift the transmission into Neutral and make sure the 4WD
indicator on the instrument cluster comes
on when you use the transfer lever to shift
into 4-wheel drive high range position
("4H") and goes off when you use the
transfer lever to shift into 2-wheel high
drive position ("2H") with the engine running. If the 4WD indicator does not come
on or it does not go off, that means, the airlocking
hubs
cannot
be
locked
or
unlocked, the vehicle must be towed with
the front wheels lifted and the rear wheels
on a dolly.

If your vehicle is disabled, and if the steering and drive train are in good condition
(and the engine can be started for 4WD
vehicles), the vehicle can be towed

Your vehicle may be towed by a tow truck
with the rear wheels lifted and the front
wheels on the ground. Towing speed
should not exceed 90 km/h (55 mph).
For this type of towing:

### 1) Shift the manual transmission to Neu-

tral or the automatic transmission to "P"
position and start the. engine.

### 3) Make sure the 4WD indicator on the
`suzuki_jimny_en_d49f4254` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:386 | doc_type:owners_manual

NOTICE
If the air-locking hubs cannot be
unlocked, tow the vehicle with the
rear wheels lifted and a dolly under

### 4) Turn the ignition key to the "ACC" posi-
`suzuki_jimny_en_7ed1cda0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:386 | doc_type:owners_manual
tion to stop the engine and to unlock

transmitted from the front wheels

Engine trouble: Starter does
not operate

### 1) Try turning the ignition switch to
`suzuki_jimny_en_9c7236fe` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
"START" position with the headlights
turned on to determine the lead-acid
battery condition. If the headlights go
excessively dim or go off, it usually
means that either the lead-acid battery
is discharged or the battery terminal
contact is poor. Recharge the lead-acid
battery or correct battery terminal contact as necessary.

### 2) If the headlights remain bright, check
`suzuki_jimny_en_007d9257` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
the fuses. If the reason for failure of the
starter is not obvious, there may be a
major electrical problem. Have the vehicle inspected by a SUZUKI dealer.
Engine trouble: Does not start
Make sure that your vehicle has enough б
fuel and battery.

### If the engine does not start under very cold
`suzuki_jimny_en_6657f842` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
condition, press the accelerator pedal all
the way to the fioor and hold it while cranking the engine.
Refer to "Starting engine" in operating your
vehicle section.

### If the engine still does not start have your
`suzuki_jimny_en_675a1a5c` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
vehicle inspected at a SUZUKI dealer.
Do not operate the starter motor for
more than 12 seconds.

### EMERGENCY SERVICE
`suzuki_jimny_en_4905a90b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
Engine trouble: Overheating
The engine could overheat temporarily
under severe driving conditions. If the high
engine coolant temperature warning light
comes on as overheating or the engine
coolant temperature gauge indicates overheating during driving:

### 2) Take the vehicle to a safe place and
`suzuki_jimny_en_d2ab169d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
park.
3) Run the engine at a normal idle speed
for a few minutes until the high engine
coolant temperature warning light goes
off or the indicator is within the normal,
acceptable temperature range between
"H" and "C".

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_eace7131` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
If you see or hear escaping steam,
stop the vehicle in a safe place and
immediately turn off the engine to
cool it. Do not open the hood when
steam is present. When the steam
can no longer be seen or heard, open
the hood to see if the coolant is still
boiling. If it is, you must wait until it
stops boiling before you proceed.
7-10

### If the high engine coolant temperature
`suzuki_jimny_en_edaa318b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:388 | doc_type:owners_manual
warning light does not go off or the temperature indication does not come down to
within the normal, acceptable range:

### 1) Turn off the engine and check that the
`suzuki_jimny_en_93faa07e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:388 | doc_type:owners_manual
water pump belt and pulleys are not
damaged or slipping. If any abnormality
is found, correct it.

### 2) Check the coolant level in the reservoir.
`suzuki_jimny_en_9e88dc3d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:hvac | p:388 | doc_type:owners_manual
If it is found to be lower than "LOW"
line, check radiator, water pump, radiator hoses and heater hoses for leakage.

### If leakage that may cause overheating
`suzuki_jimny_en_fdb22fdc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:388 | doc_type:owners_manual
is found, do not run the engine until
these problems have been corrected.

### 3) If leakage is not found, carefully add
`suzuki_jimny_en_a76f6608` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:388 | doc_type:owners_manual
coolant to the reservoir and then the
radiator, if necessary. (Refer to "Engine
coolant" in "INSPECTION AND MAIN-
TENANCE" section.)

### If engine overheats and you are not sure
`suzuki_jimny_en_dbc55dff` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:388 | doc_type:owners_manual
what to do, contact a SUZUKI dealer.

• It is hazardous to remove the radiator cap when the water temperature
is high, because scalding fluid and
