`suzuki_jimny_en_b0d8032b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:353 | doc_type:owners_manual
each brake and requires the use of a
micrometer or caliper, which must be done
according to the instructions described in
the relevant service manual or available
from the relevant repair information site.

### Steering wheel play
`suzuki_jimny_en_935ead0a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:353 | doc_type:owners_manual
11c":
0- 30 mm (0.0 -1.2 in.)
Check the free play of the steering wheel
by gently turning it from left to right and
measuring the distance that it moves
before you feel slight resistance. The play
should be between the specified values.

### Check that the steering wheel turns easily
`suzuki_jimny_en_722408ec` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:353 | doc_type:owners_manual
and smoothly without rattling by turning it
all the way to the right and to the left while
driving very slowly in an open area. If the
amount of free play is not as specified or
you find anything else to be wrong, an
inspection must be performed by a
SUZUKI dealer.

### INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE
`suzuki_jimny_en_49d511b7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:353 | doc_type:owners_manual
Tyres
78RB07013
The front and rear tyre pressure specifications are listed in the tyre information label.

### Both front and rear tyres should have the
`suzuki_jimny_en_935f6d80` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:353 | doc_type:owners_manual
specified tyre pressure.
NOTE:
The tyre pressure will change due to
changes in atmospheric pressure, temperature or tyre temperature when driving.

### To reduce the chance that the low tyre
`suzuki_jimny_en_44bad628` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:353 | doc_type:owners_manual
pressure warning light (if equipped) will
come on due to normal changes in temperature and atmospheric pressure, it is
important to check and adjust the tyre
pressures when the tyres are cold. If you
check tyres after driving, they are warm.

### Even if the tyre pressure seems to be good
`suzuki_jimny_en_83d25b14` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:353 | doc_type:owners_manual
in this condition, it could fall below the
6-36
INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE
specified pressure when tyres cool down.
Also, tyres that are inflated to the specified
pressure in a warm garage may have pressure below the specification when the vehi-
cle
is driven
outside in
very cold
temperature. If you adjust the tyre pressure in a garage that is warmer than the
outside temperature, you should add 1 kPa
to the recommended cold tyre pressure for
every O.B'C difference between garage
temperature and outside temperature.
6-37

### Tyre inspection
`suzuki_jimny_en_910071e7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:354 | doc_type:owners_manual
Inspect your vehicle's tyres at least once a
month or before long trip by performing the
following checks:

### 1) Measure the air pressure with a tyre
`suzuki_jimny_en_413fffbf` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:354 | doc_type:owners_manual
gauge. Adjust the pressure if necessary. Remember to check the spare
tyre, too.

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_51603c26` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:354 | doc_type:owners_manual
• Air pressures should be checked
when the tyres are cold or you may
get inaccurate readings.

### Check the inflation pressure from
`suzuki_jimny_en_0ec6f169` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:354 | doc_type:owners_manual
time to time while inflating the tyre
gradually, until the specified pressure is obtained.
Never under-inflate or over-inflate
the tyres.
Under-inflation can cause unusual
handling characteristics or can
cause the rim to slip on the tyre
bead, resulting in an accident or
damage to the tyre or rim.
Over-inflation can cause the lyre to
burst, resulting in personal injury.
Over-inflation
can
also
cause
unusual handling characteristics
which may result in an accident.

### 78RB07048
`suzuki_jimny_en_74c73093` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:354 | doc_type:owners_manual
(1) Tread wear indicator
(2) Indicator location mark

### 2) Check that the depth of the tread
`suzuki_jimny_en_a7c88cb2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:354 | doc_type:owners_manual
groove is more than 1.6 mm (0.06 in.).
To help you check this, the tyres have
molded-in tread wear indicators in the
grooves. When the indicators appear
on the tread surface, the remaining
depth of the tread is 1.6 mm (0.06 in.)
or less and the tyre should be replaced.

### 3) Check for abnormal wear, cracks and
`suzuki_jimny_en_2100abfd` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:354 | doc_type:owners_manual
damage. Any tyres with cracks or other
damage should be replaced. If any
tyres show abnormal wear, have them
inspected by a SUZUKI dealer.

### Hitting curbs and running over rocks
`suzuki_jimny_en_0a6e4d1e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:355 | doc_type:owners_manual
can damage tyres and affect wheel
alignment.
Have tyres
and wheel
alignment checked periodically by a
SUZUKI dealer.

### 5) Check that there are no nails, stones or
`suzuki_jimny_en_a3aa737a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:355 | doc_type:owners_manual
other objects sticking into the tyres.
A WARNING
• Your SUZUKI vehicle is equipped
with tyres which are all the same
type and size. This is important to
ensure proper steering and handling
of the vehicle.

### Never mix
`suzuki_jimny_en_3c69c4db` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:355 | doc_type:owners_manual
tyres of different size or type on the
four wheels of your vehicle. The
size and type of tyres used should
be only those approved by SUZUKI
as standard or optional equipment
for your vehicle.

### Replacing the wheels and tyres
`suzuki_jimny_en_7421a7d2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:steering | p:355 | doc_type:owners_manual
equipped on your vehicle with certain combinations
of aftermarket
wheels and tyres can significantly
change the steering and handling
characteristics of your vehicle.
Therefore, use only those wheel
and tyre combinations approved by

### SUZUKI as standard or optional
`suzuki_jimny_en_88a718ee` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:355 | doc_type:owners_manual
equipment for your vehicle.
NOTICE
Replacing the original tyres with
tyres of a different size may result
in false speedometer or odometer
readings.

### Check with a SUZUKI
`suzuki_jimny_en_841769bb` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:355 | doc_type:owners_manual
dealer before purchasing replacement tyres that differ in size from
the original tyres.
Replacing a tyre with one of a different
size, or
using different
brands among the four tyres can
result in damage to the drive train.

### 78RB07014
`suzuki_jimny_en_5fa9c549` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
To change a wheel, use the following procedure:
1) Remove the jack, tools and spare
wheel from the vehicle.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_4dd246c4` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
How to remove the spare wheel:
78RB07052
1. Remove the center nut (1 ), then
remove the spare wheel half cover
(2) (if equipped).

### 2. Remove the wheel nuts of the spare
`suzuki_jimny_en_56b19fc8` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
wheel, then remove the spare wheel
with both hands.

### 2) Loosen, but do not remove the wheel
`suzuki_jimny_en_18428bbc` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
nuts.
3) Jack up the vehicle (follow the jacking
instructions in the "EMERGENCY SER-
VICE" section in this manual)

### 5) Before installing the new wheel, clean
`suzuki_jimny_en_2c1c8f3c` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:356 | doc_type:owners_manual
any mud or dirt off from the surface of
the wheel and hub with a clean cloth.
Clean the hub carefully; it may be hot
from driving.

### 6) Install the new wheel and replace the
`suzuki_jimny_en_f24ee856` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
wheel nuts with their cone shaped end
facing the wheel. Tighten each nut
snugly by hand until the wheel is
securely seated on the hub.

### 78RB07017
`suzuki_jimny_en_06533e31` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
Tightening torque for wheel nut:
100 Nm (10.0 kg-m, 72.3 lb-ft)

### 7) Lower the jack and fully tighten the nuts
`suzuki_jimny_en_1bd37bd4` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
in a crisscross fashion with a wrench as
shown in the illustration.

### Use genuine wheel nuts and tighten
`suzuki_jimny_en_9514e50a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
them to the specified torque as soon
as possible after changing wheels.

### Incorrect wheel nuts or improperly
`suzuki_jimny_en_6ec53865` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:357 | doc_type:owners_manual
tightened wheel nuts may come
loose or fall off, which can result in
an accident. If you do not have a
torque wrench, have the wheel nut
torque checked by a SUZUKI dealer.

### NOTE:

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_95a8c903` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:358 | doc_type:owners_manual
• Batteries
produce
flammable
hydrogen gas. Keep flames and
sparks away from the battery or an
explosion may occur. Never smoke
when working near the battery.
• When checking or servicing the
battery, disconnect the negative
cable. Be careful not to cause a
short circuit by allowing metal
objects to contact the battery posts
and the vehicle at the same time.
To avoid harm to yourself or damage to your vehicle or battery, fol-
low the jump-starting instructions
in "EMERGENCY SERVICE" section if it is necessary to jump-start
your vehicle.
• Diluted sulfuric acid spilled from
battery can cause blindness or
severe burns. Use proper eye protection and gloves. Flush eyes or
bodi,: with ample water and get
medical care immediately if suffered. Keep batteries out of reach
of children.

### Batteries contain toxic substances
`suzuki_jimny_en_cea750c7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual
including sulfuric acid and lead. They
could have potential negative consequences for the environment and
human health. Used batteries must
be disposed of or recycled according
to applicable rules or regulations and
must not be disposed of with ordinary household trash. Make sure not
to tip over the battery when you
remove it from the vehicle. Otherwise, sulfuric acid could run out and
you might get injury.

chemical symbol of "Pb" (6) indicates the
battery contains more than 0.004% lead.

`suzuki_jimny_en_96b9abbb` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:359 | doc_type:owners_manual

used battery, consult a SUZUKI dealer.

load groups.

### Always replace a blown fuse with a
`suzuki_jimny_en_681e6a49` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:363 | doc_type:owners_manual
fuse of the correct amperage. Never
use a substitute such as aluminum
foil or wire to replace a blown fuse. If
you replace a fuse and the new one
blows in a short period of time, you
may have a major electrical problem.
Have your vehicle inspected immediately by a SUZUKI dealer.

### Light bulbs can be hot enough to
`suzuki_jimny_en_b5ad5ffe` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
burn your finger right after turning
off lights. This is true especially for
halogen headlight bulbs. Replace
the bulbs after they become cool
enough.

### The headlight bulbs are filled with
`suzuki_jimny_en_245999c3` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
pressurized halogen gas. They can
burst and injure you if they are hit
or dropped. Handle them carefully.

### To avoid
`suzuki_jimny_en_aee9283d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
injury
by sharp-edged
parts of the body, wear gloves and
a long-sleeved shirt when replacing
light bulbs.

### The oils from your skin may cause a
`suzuki_jimny_en_339193f2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
halogen bulb to overheat and burst
when the lights are on. Grasp a new
bulb with a clean cloth.

### Frequent bulb replacement indicates
`suzuki_jimny_en_742fe7db` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:364 | doc_type:owners_manual
the need for an inspection of the electrical system. This should be carried
out by a SUZUKI dealer.

`suzuki_jimny_en_d8868a8e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:374 | doc_type:owners_manual

Jacking instructions
75F062
1) Place the vehicle on level, hard ground.

### 2) Set the parking brake firmly and shift
`suzuki_jimny_en_dc2fcfd3` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:brakes | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
into "P" (Park) if your vehicle has an
automatic transmission, or shift int6 "R"
(Reverse) if your vehicle has a manual
transmission.

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_9b7687e2` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:drivetrain | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
Shift into "P" (Park) for an automatic
transmission, or into "R" (Reverse)
for a manual transmission vehicle
when you jack up the vehicle.
• Never jack up the vehicle with the
transmission in
11N" (Neutral). Otherwise, unstable jack may cause an
accident.

### 3) Turn on the hazard warning switch if
`suzuki_jimny_en_c24a6054` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
your vehicle is near traffic.
4) Block the front and rear of the wheel
diagonally opposite of the wheel being
lifted.

### 5) Place the spare wheel near the wheel
`suzuki_jimny_en_cd6c58df` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:378 | doc_type:owners_manual
being lifted as shown in the illustration
in case that the jack is slipped.
Front wheel/Rear wheel

### 54G277
`suzuki_jimny_en_533f3df6` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:379 | doc_type:owners_manual
(1) Boss
6) Position the jack vertically and raise the
jack by turning the jack handle clockwise until the jack head hole fits into the
boss (1) of the body as the illustration.

### 7) Continue to raise the jack slowly and
`suzuki_jimny_en_547cbe6b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:379 | doc_type:owners_manual
smoothly until the tyre clears the
ground. Do not raise the vehicle more
than necessary.

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_800b8684` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:379 | doc_type:owners_manual
• Use the jack only to change wheels
on level, hard ground.
• Never jack up the vehicle on an
inclined surface.
• Never raise the vehicle with the
jack
in
a location
other
than
between the frame bosses near the
wheel to be changed.
• Make sure that the jack is raised at
least 51 mm (2 inches) before it
contacts the boss. Use of the jack
when it is within 51 mm (2 inches)
of being fully collapsed may result
in failure of the jack.
No person should place any portion of their body under a vehicle
that is supported by a jack.
• Never run the engine when the
vehicle is supported
by the jack
and never allow
passengers
to
remain in the vehicle.

Jump-starting instructions

### A. WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_15887e53` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
Never attempt to jump-start your
vehicle
if the
lead-acid
battery
appears to be frozen. Batteries in
this condition may explode.
When making jump lead connections, check that your hands and
the jump leads remain clear from
pulleys, belts or fans.
Lead-acid batteries produce flammable hydrogen gas. Keep flames
and sparks away from the battery
or an explosion may occur. Never
smoke when working near the battery.

### If the booster battery you use for
`suzuki_jimny_en_022d07ba` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
jump-starting is installed in another
vehicle, check that the two vehicles
are not touching each other.
If your lead-acid battery discharges
repeatedly, for no apparent reason,
have your vehicle inspected by a
SUZUKI dealer.
• To avoid harm to yourself or damage to your vehicle or battery, fol-
low the jump-starting
instructions
below.
If you are in doubt, call for qualified
road service.

### Your vehicle should not be started by
`suzuki_jimny_en_79a88abd` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
pushing
or towing.
This
starting
method could result in permanent
damage to the catalytic converter.

### Use jump leads to start a vehicle with
`suzuki_jimny_en_6a214e20` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
a weak or flat battery.
1) Use only a 12-volt lead-acid battery to
jump-start your vehicle. Position the
good 12-volt lead-acid battery close to
your vehicle so that the jump leads will
reach both batteries. When using a battery installed on another vehicle, check
that two vehicles do not touch each
other. Set the parking brakes fully on
both vehicles.

### 2) Turn off all vehicle accessories, except
`suzuki_jimny_en_5e55e03d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:382 | doc_type:owners_manual
those necessary for safety reasons (for
example, headlights or hazard lights).

### 1. Connect one end of the first jump
`suzuki_jimny_en_a7c2800f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
lead to the positive (+) terminal of
the discharged battery (1 ).

### 2. Connect the other end to the positive
`suzuki_jimny_en_10db6f74` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
(+) terminal of the booster battery
(2).
3. Connect one end of the second jump
lead to the negative (-) terminal of
the booster battery (2).

### 4. Make the final connection to an
`suzuki_jimny_en_e43796a9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
unpainted metal part (3) of engine
cylinder head in the vehicle with the
discharged battery (1 ).

### Never connect the jump lead directly
`suzuki_jimny_en_31121ea5` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
to the negative (-) terminal of the discharged battery, or an explosion may
occur.

### 4) If the booster battery you are using is
`suzuki_jimny_en_7e411bff` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
fitted to another vehicle, start the
engine of the vehicle with the booster
battery. Run the engine at moderate
speed.

### 5) Start the engine of the vehicle with the
`suzuki_jimny_en_c661eb53` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:383 | doc_type:owners_manual
discharged battery.
6) Remove the jump leads in the exact
reverse order in which you connected
them.

Engine trouble: Starter does
not operate

### 1) Try turning the ignition switch to
`suzuki_jimny_en_9c7236fe` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
"START" position with the headlights
turned on to determine the lead-acid
battery condition. If the headlights go
excessively dim or go off, it usually
means that either the lead-acid battery
is discharged or the battery terminal
contact is poor. Recharge the lead-acid
battery or correct battery terminal contact as necessary.

### 2) If the headlights remain bright, check
`suzuki_jimny_en_007d9257` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual

starter is not obvious, there may be a
major electrical problem. Have the vehicle inspected by a SUZUKI dealer.

fuel and battery.

Engine trouble: Overheating
The engine could overheat temporarily
under severe driving conditions. If the high
engine coolant temperature warning light
comes on as overheating or the engine
coolant temperature gauge indicates overheating during driving:

### 2) Take the vehicle to a safe place and
`suzuki_jimny_en_d2ab169d` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual

coolant temperature warning light goes
off or the indicator is within the normal,
acceptable temperature range between
"H" and "C".

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_eace7131` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:387 | doc_type:owners_manual
If you see or hear escaping steam,
stop the vehicle in a safe place and
immediately turn off the engine to
cool it. Do not open the hood when
steam is present. When the steam
can no longer be seen or heard, open
the hood to see if the coolant is still
boiling. If it is, you must wait until it
stops boiling before you proceed.

TENANCE" section.)

### CARE
`suzuki_jimny_en_2b4893f7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:389 | doc_type:owners_manual
Corrosion prevention .......................................................... 8-1

### Corrosion prevention
`suzuki_jimny_en_3e06c6ef` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
It is_ important to take good care of your
vehicle to protect it from corrosion. Listed
below are instructions for how to maintain
your vehicle to prevent corrosion. Please
read and follow these instructions carefully.
Important information about corrosion

### 1) Accumulation of road salt, dirt moisture
`suzuki_jimny_en_31121165` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
or chemicals in hard-to-reach areas of
the vehicle underbody or frame.

### 2) Chipping, scratches and any damage to
`suzuki_jimny_en_b8f4fab1` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
treated
or painted
metal surfaces
resulting from minor accidents or abrasion by stones and gravel.
Environmental conditions which accelerate corrosion

### 1) Road salt, dust control chemicals, sea
`suzuki_jimny_en_8f15ba78` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
breeze or industrial pollution will all
accelerate the corrosion of metal.

### 2) High humidity will increase the rate of
`suzuki_jimny_en_65272712` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
corrosion particularly when the temperature range is just above the freez-
ing point.

### 3) Moisture in certain areas of a vehicle
`suzuki_jimny_en_a4c20883` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
for an extended period of lime may promote corrosion even though other body
sections may be completely dry.
8-1

### 4) High temperatures will cause an accel-
`suzuki_jimny_en_4e058f07` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:hvac | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
erated rate of corrosion to parts of the
vehicle which are not well-ventilated to
permit quick drying.

### This information illustrates the necessity of
`suzuki_jimny_en_f130a609` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
keeping your vehicle
(particularly the
~nderbody) as clean and dry as possible. It

### Is equally important to repair any damage
`suzuki_jimny_en_68d18168` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
to the paint or protective coatings as soon
as possible.

### Wash your vehicle frequently
`suzuki_jimny_en_e21a647e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
The_ best way to preserve the finish on your
vehicle and to help avoid corrosion is to
keep it clean with frequent washing.

### Wash your vehicle at least once during the
`suzuki_jimny_en_3ca23f49` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
winter and once immediately after the winter. K<:ep your vehicle, particularly the
underside, as clean and dry as possible.

### If you frequently drive on salted roads
`suzuki_jimny_en_57cb4a00` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
your vehicle should be washed at least
once a month during the winter. If you live
near the ocean, your vehicle should be
washed at least once a month throughout
the year.
For washing instructions, refer to "Vehicle
cleaning" section.

### Foreign materials such as salts chemicals
`suzuki_jimny_en_b014d34e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
road oil or tar, tree sap, bird droppings and
industnal fall-out may damage the finish of
your vehicle if it is left on painted surfaces.

### Remove these types of deposits as quickly
`suzuki_jimny_en_a41314ab` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
as possible. If these deposits are difficult to
wash off, an additional cleaner may be
required. Check that any cleaner you use
is not harmful to painted surfaces and is
specifically intended for your purposes.
Follow the manufacturer's directions when
using these special cleaners.

### Carefully examine your vehicle for damage
`suzuki_jimny_en_9df35173` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:390 | doc_type:owners_manual
to the painted surfaces. Should you find
any chip~ or scratches in the paint, touch
them up 1mmed1ately to prevent corrosion
from starting. If the chips or scratches have
gone through to the bare metal have a
qualified body shop make the rep~ir.
Keep passenger and luggage compartments clean
Moisture, dirt or mud can accumulate
under the floor mats and may cause corrosion. Occasionally, check under these
mats to ensure that this area is clean and
dry. More fr~quent checks are necessary if
the vehicle Is used for off-road driving or in
wet weather.
Certain cargos such as chemicals, fertilizers, cleaners, salts, etc. are extremely cor-
rosive by nature. These products should
be transported in sealed containers. If they
are spilled or leaked, clean and dry the
area immediately.
Park your vehicle in a dry, well-ventilated area
Do not park your vehicle in a damp, poorlyventilated area. If you often wash your
vehicle in the garage and place it there in
wet condition, your garage may be damp.

### The high humidity in the garage may
`suzuki_jimny_en_6c6c1d3f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:hvac | p:391 | doc_type:owners_manual
cause or accelerate corrosion. A wet vehicle may corrode even in a heated garage if
the ventilation is poor.

### The use of mud and gravel shields will help
`suzuki_jimny_en_428ed747` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:391 | doc_type:owners_manual
protect your vehicle, especially if you frequently drive on gravel or salted roads.
Full-size shields, which extend as close to
the road as is practical, are the best. The
fittings for such shields should also be corrosion resistant. Please check with your

### SUZUKI dealer for information on these
`suzuki_jimny_en_ff524525` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:391 | doc_type:owners_manual
shields.
A WARNING
Do not apply additional undercoating
or rust preventive coating on or
around exhaust system components
such as the catalytic converter and
exhaust pipes. A fire could be started
if
the
undercoating
substance
becomes overheated.

### When cleaning the interior or exterior
`suzuki_jimny_en_8d5a736f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:391 | doc_type:owners_manual
of the vehicle, do not use flammable
solvents such as lacquer thinners,
gasoline and benzene. Also, do not
use cleaning
materials
such as
bleaches
and
strong
household
detergents.
The
materials
could
cause personal injury or damage to
the vehicle.
8-2

### Vinyl upholstery
`suzuki_jimny_en_385d647a` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
Prepare a solution of soap or mild detergent dissolved in warm water. Apply the
solution to the vinyl with a sponge or soft
cloth and let it soak for a few minutes to
loosen dirt.
б
Rub the surface with a clean, damp cloth
to remove dirt and the soap solution. If
some dirt still remains on the surface,
repeat this procedure.

### Fabric upholstery
`suzuki_jimny_en_103161a7` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
Remove loose dirt with a vacuum cleaner.
Using a mild soap solution, rub stained
areas with a clean damp cloth. To remove
soap, rub the areas again with a cloth
dampened with water. Repeat this until the
stain is removed, or use a commercial fabric cleaner for tougher stains. If you use a
fabric cleaner, carefully follow the manufacturer's instructions and precautions.

### Leather upholstery
`suzuki_jimny_en_b0caf37b` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
Remove loose dirt with a vacuum cleaner.
Using a mild soap or saddle soap solution,
wipe dirt off with a clean damp soft cloth.
To remove soap, wipe the areas again with
a soft cloth dampened with water. Wipe the
areas dry with a soft dry cloth. Repeat this
until the dirt or stain is removed, or use a
commercial leather cleaner for tougher dirt
or stains. If you use a leather cleaner,
carefully follow the manufacturer's instructions and precautions. Do not use solvent
type cleaners or abrasive cleaners.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_591cb7c9` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
In order to keep leather upholstery looking good, it should be cleaned at least
twice a year.

### If leather
`suzuki_jimny_en_edce2308` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
upholstery becomes
wet,
immediately wipe it dry with tissue paper
or a soft cloth. Water may cause leather
to harden and shrink if it is not wiped off.
When parking on sunny days, select a
shady place or use a sunshade. If
leather upholstery is exposed to direct
sunlight for a long time, it may disco/or
and shrink.
As is common with natural materials,
leather is inherently irregular in grain and
cowhide has spots in its natural state.

### These do not affect the performance of
`suzuki_jimny_en_5a359097` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
the leather in any way.
Seat belts
Clean seat belts with a mild soap and
water. Do not use bleach or dye on the
belts. They may weaken the fabric in the
belts.

### Ordinary dirt can be removed from vinyl
`suzuki_jimny_en_ec71ccdf` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
with water or mild soap. Use a brush to
help loosen dirt. After the dirt is loosened,
rinse the mat thoroughly wtth water and
dry it in the shade.

### Remove dirt and soil as much as possible
`suzuki_jimny_en_aa6685c0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
with a vacuum cleaner. Using a mild soap
solution, rub stained areas with a clean
damp cloth. To remove soap, rub the areas
again with a cloth dampened with water.
Repeat this until the stain is removed, or
use a commercial carpet cleaner for
tougher stains. If you use a carpet cleaner,
carefully follow the manufacturer's instructions and precautions.

### Instrument panel and console
`suzuki_jimny_en_29d859bd` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:392 | doc_type:owners_manual
Remove loose dirt with a vacuum cleaner.
Gently wipe dirt off with a tightly squeezed
damp clean cloth. Repeat this until the dirt
is removed.

### Do not use chemical products that
`suzuki_jimny_en_357153c0` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:infotainment | p:393 | doc_type:owners_manual
contain silicon to wipe electrical
components such as the air conditioning system, audio 1
navigation
system, or other switches. These will
cause damage to the components.

### NOTICE
`suzuki_jimny_en_c5d7e88f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:393 | doc_type:owners_manual
Liquid such as liquid aromatics,
soft drinks or juice may cause discoloration, wrinkles, and cracking
to resin-based parts and textiles.

### Immediately wipe it dry with tissue
`suzuki_jimny_en_166c0334` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:393 | doc_type:owners_manual
paper or a soft cloth.
Do not leave leather products with
color, fur or vinyl products, etc. in
your vehicle for long periods. It
may cause discoloration or deterioration of interior.

### Cleaning
`suzuki_jimny_en_a6dfc07f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:393 | doc_type:owners_manual
exterior
NOTICE
It is important that your vehicle be
kept clean and free from dirt. Failure
to keep your vehicle clean may result
in fading of the paint or corrosion to
various parts of the vehicle body.

### NOTE:
`suzuki_jimny_en_905cbc46` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:393 | doc_type:owners_manual
Do not use an acidic or alkaline detergent, or a cleaner containing petroleum
solvent to wash aluminum wheels.
These types of cleaner will cause permanent spots, disco/oration and cracks
on finished surfaces and damage to center caps.
Do not use a bristle brush and soap containing an abrasive material. These will
damage finished surfaces.

### Never attempt to wash and wax
`suzuki_jimny_en_9cce276e` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:engine | p:393 | doc_type:owners_manual
your vehicle with the engine running.
When cleaning the underside of the
body and fender, where there may
be sharp-edged parts, wear gloves
and a long-sleeved shirt to protect
your hands and arms from being
cut.
After washing your vehicle, carefully test the brakes before driving
to check that they have maintained
their normal effectiveness.

### The fuel tank has an air space to
`suzuki_jimny_en_a3ad8982` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:lighting | p:399 | doc_type:owners_manual

expansion
in hot

after the filler nozzle has automatically shut off or an initial blowback
occurs, the air chamber will become
full. Exposure to heat when fully
fuelled in this manner will result in
leakage due to fuel expansion. To
prevent such fuel leakage, stop filling
after the filler nozzle has automatically shut off, or when initial vent
blowback occurs, if using an alternative non-automatic system.

not covered under the New Vehicle
Limited Warranty.

### Seat belt warning
`suzuki_jimny_en_b0d58fea` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:410 | doc_type:owners_manual
Follow this warning as well as the instruction for seat belt in this book.

### Seat belts are designed to bear upon
`suzuki_jimny_en_b9667eb1` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:body | p:410 | doc_type:owners_manual
the bony structure of the body, and
should be worn low across the front
of the pelvis or the pelvis, chest and
shoulders, as applicable; wearing the
lap section of the belt across the
abdominal area must be avoided.
• Seat belts should be adjusted as
firmly as possible, consistent with
comfort, to provide the protection
for which they have been designed.

### A slack belt will greatly reduce the
`suzuki_jimny_en_d1cfbc9f` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:ev | p:410 | doc_type:owners_manual
protection afforded to the wearer.
• Care should be taken to avoid contamination of the webbing with pol-
ishes, oils and chemicals, and
particularly
battery acid. Cleaning
may safely be carried out using
mild soap and water. The belt
should
be replaced
if webbing
becomes frayed, contaminated or
damaged.
(Continued)

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_8bf8b6d1` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:general | p:410 | doc_type:owners_manual
(Continued)
• It is essential to replace the entire
assembly after it has been worn in
a severe impact even if damage to
the assembly is not obvious.

### Belts should
`suzuki_jimny_en_20969037` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:410 | doc_type:owners_manual
not be worn with
straps twisted.
Each belt assembly must only be
used by one occupant; it is dangerous to put a belt around a child
being carried on the occupant's
lap,
In the case where a "Seat Belt Assembly''
incorporates an "Automatic Length Adjusting and Locking Retractor' or an "Emer-
gency Locking Retractor'.

### A WARNING
`suzuki_jimny_en_8bf8b6d1` | jimny | pdf_manual | tier:2 | lang:en | layer:interior | p:410 | doc_type:owners_manual
No
modifications
or
additions
should be made by the user which
will either prevent the seat belt
adjusting devices from operating to
remove slack, or prevent the seat
belt assembly from being adjusted
to remove slack.
